input_references.role: Timestamped GPS trajectory points linked by trajectory_id

metadata.goal: Investigate spatial and mobility differences among weekday work trajectories with different destination locations.
metadata.category: Weekday work trajectories divided into central-bound and outward flows, with destination location, departure time, transport mode, route corridor, and point-level GPS data.
metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 17 Weekday Work Destination Flows
metadata.dataset_description: Weekday work trajectories divided into central-bound and outward flows, with destination location, departure time, transport mode, route corridor, and point-level GPS data.
metadata.metric_note: Distances are calculated from delivered GPS polylines; average point speed and duration are synchronized with the point table. Montréal's long island axis runs approximately southwest–northeast, so signed axis displacement summarizes the dominant travel direction.

plot.title: Central-bound and Outward Work Flows
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: What shares of weekday work trajectories flow toward central versus peripheral employment?
insight_list.insight: Morning work trajectories show a strong inward flow toward central employment areas, while a smaller outward-flow group ends in peripheral employment zones.

plot.title: Mode and Distance by Work-flow Group
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How do mode composition and distance differ between central-bound and outward work trips?
insight_list.insight: Outward commuters rely more on motor vehicles and travel longer distances; central-bound commuters include more public-transit and cycling trajectories.

plot.title: Departure Time and Corridor Reuse
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Do outward trips depart earlier and reuse fewer corridors more intensively?
insight_list.insight: Outward work trips depart earlier and follow fewer recurring radial corridors, producing greater route overlap than central-bound work trips.

plot.title: Short Active-mode Outward Exceptions
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Which outward work trips depart from the usual motorized, longer-distance pattern?
insight_list.insight: A few short outward commutes near peripheral employment zones use walking or cycling, forming exceptions to the otherwise motorized pattern

insights: Morning work trajectories show a strong inward flow toward central employment areas, while a smaller outward-flow group ends in peripheral employment zones.
Outward commuters rely more on motor vehicles and travel longer distances; central-bound commuters include more public-transit and cycling trajectories.
Outward work trips depart earlier and follow fewer recurring radial corridors, producing greater route overlap than central-bound work trips.
A few short outward commutes near peripheral employment zones use walking or cycling, forming exceptions to the otherwise motorized pattern
summary: Most weekday work trips flow inward to central employment and use a diverse mode mix. Outward commuters leave earlier, travel farther, rely more on motor vehicles, and repeatedly share a small corridor set; four short active trips form clear local exceptions.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this controlled constructed dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
